overrideAnalysis.question: this run carries the corpus highest override rate (64% + detached candidates). What did that do to a pipeline built on component mappings?
overrideAnalysis.headline: NOTHING - because the override rate never reached the mapping layer. 0 of 21 Code Connect probes resolved, so the mapping layer expressed nothing about ANY of the 57 live instances. The binding constraint is upstream of overrides.

codeConnect.note: subtree {} AND per-node {} agree here - unlike earlier runs where the subtree lied and per-node calls returned real mappings. This design is genuinely unconnected everywhere.

instancesCarryingOverridesAMappingCouldN.caveat: trivially 100%, and that is the finding: with a zero denominator of mappings, override rate is not a property the pipeline can even observe. A 64% override rate and a 0% override rate would have produced the identical run.

whatThePipelineDidWithThem: the copy-pasted active state became a [data-active] boolean on one component, not a second component or a variant
the 3 icon paths collapsed to ONE predicate: is the glyph in the theme 34-icon registry? yes -> <sl-icon>, no -> iconGap() reserved footprint
the detached sl-select container became a plain controlled <ul> whose expansion and selection are owned by the root
every visual difference was modelled as a property on our own component, because nothing in the file carries authoritative variant information
overrideAnalysis.mappingValidButWrong: NOT APPLICABLE and recorded as such rather than guessed: with 0 resolved mappings there is nothing whose output could be compared against the design. This is the honest answer to the batch question for this case.
